options: Divides the ordered rows into 4 roughly equal groups, numbered 1 through 4
Ranks rows individually, same as RANK()
Removes duplicate rows, keeping only 4 per group
Returns only the top 4 rows
questions.explain: NTILE splits an ordered result set into a fixed number of buckets, unlike RANK/DENSE_RANK which rank rows individually.

questions.q: In 'NTILE(4) OVER (ORDER BY ListPrice DESC)', which group holds the most expensive products?
options: It's unpredictable
Group 4
The group is determined by PARTITION BY only
Group 1
questions.explain: Because of the DESC order, group 1 is filled first with the highest-priced rows.

questions.q: What happens when the total row count isn't evenly divisible by NTILE's bucket count?
options: The extra rows are dropped from the result set entirely
All extra rows go into the last group
SQL Server raises an error
SQL Server distributes the extra rows to the earliest groups, one extra row each
questions.explain: For example, 22 rows into NTILE(4) produces groups of 6, 6, 5, 5 — no group differs by more than one row.

questions.q: Can NTILE be combined with PARTITION BY?
options: Only when using RANK() in the same query
No, NTILE cannot be partitioned
Only for numeric partition columns
Yes — it computes the buckets separately within each partition, just like other window functions this chapter
questions.explain: NTILE(4) OVER (PARTITION BY Color ORDER BY ListPrice DESC) computes quartiles separately per color.

questions.q: What real-world question is NTILE well suited for?
options: "What is the exact rank of this specific row?"
"Which price quartile does this product fall into?" — splitting data into a fixed number of equal-sized groups
"How many rows share this exact value?"
"What is the running total up to this row?"
questions.explain: NTILE is coarser than RANK/DENSE_RANK — it groups rows into buckets rather than ranking them individually.
